name: Quantoz USDQ
oneLiner: USDQ is Quantoz Payments' MiCA-authorized dollar e-money token, backed by cash, deposits, and EU and U.S. government bonds.
collateral: U.S. dollar deposits and government bonds (Netherlands, Germany, US) held in segregated, bankruptcy-remote accounts at Tier 1 European banks by Stichting Quantoz, supervised by DNB; reserve ratio disclosed on Quantoz's transparency page
pegMechanism: Direct 1:1 redemption through Quantoz Payments for onboarded customers; reserves are disclosed against circulating supply on the Quantoz transparency page

mechanismArchetypeReview.reviewer: SONG-5 Safety Score V9 mechanism review
mechanismArchetypeReview.rationale: Quantoz's USDQ disclosure describes direct 1:1 redemption for onboarded customers and a segregated reserve of cash deposits and government bonds. The disclosed 30% cash and 70% government-bond allocation supports the fiat-cash classification. The reviewed materials do not provide an independent current assurance opinion, full bank/custodian identity, or complete legal claim and insolvency treatment, so no stronger mechanism-component conclusion is made.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: Quantoz announced LayerZero and Stargate interoperability for USDQ and EURQ, starting with Ethereum-to-Polygon transfers. The route therefore depends on external LayerZero/Stargate infrastructure rather than solely issuer-native mint/redeem rails; exact adapter topology should remain under review.

genius.notes: USDQ is a Dutch MiCA EMT, but no public GENIUS foreign-issuer registration or U.S. permitted-issuer status was located. The GENIUS Act foreign-exception framework remains in proposed-rules phase as of 2026-06-18; no foreign exception registry or comparability determination has been established.

mintAuthority.summary: USDQ is issuer-minted on both Ethereum (3/5 multisig owner, no modules) and Polygon (2/5 multisig owner, no modules) via the same HadronToken onlyOwner mint function. Polygon can independently mint. Both chain proxy admins are 3/5 multisigs, no modules.

review.evidence: At ETH block 25294990: owner()=0x284Df (3/5 multisig, no modules), proxy admin=0xa6724f (3/5 multisig, no modules). At Polygon block 88323726: owner()=0x84e8d (2/5 multisig, no modules), proxy admin=0x2f875 (3/5 multisig, no modules). Polygon deployment uses same HadronToken implementation and can independently mint. XRPL and Algorand contracts not in mint-authority scope (separate ledger rails); Ethereum and Polygon are the material EVM mint surfaces.

sources.label: DNB public register - Quantoz Payments B.V.

reserveReview.rationale: Quantoz's June 30 reserve overview reports USDQ at 30% allocated cash and 70% government bonds, with a 101.23% reserve ratio. The USDQ whitepaper confirms that at least 30% is held in separate bank accounts and the remainder in secure, low-risk, highly liquid instruments; the dashboard identifies the bond issuers as the Netherlands, Germany, and United States.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Quantoz Reserve Status Overview updated June 30, 2026
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The two disclosed categories cover the full reserve allocation, but Quantoz does not identify individual banking partners, bond security identifiers, country weights, or a maximum maturity. Liquidity horizon therefore remains unknown for the government-bond bucket.
